h1: The 5 Best Armless Task Chairs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Armless Task Chairs 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 armless task chairs scored on seat comfort, back support, adjustability and small-space fit, priced from $25 to $100.
summary: The Amazon Basics Low-Back Armless chair is the safe all-round pick, with pneumatic height adjustment, a 360-degree swivel and a back-support design. The Serta Armless mesh chair is the cooler alternative, and the Orange Factory Criss Cross is the one to buy if you sit cross-legged. OLIXIS and DUMOS are the cheapest ways to fit a seat under a small desk.
intro: Armless chairs get bought for one reason: the desk is too low or too crowded for armrests. Then buyers discover the real tradeoff, which is that without arms, your forearms need a desk that supports them, and a low back that stops under the shoulder blades does little for a long day. Armless is a clearance choice, not a comfort upgrade, and the right pick depends on how you sit.

Primea editors reviewed the armless task chairs whose listings state that design, and ranked them on seat shape, back support, height adjustment and how well each suits a small or shared workspace. All five sit between $25 and $100, so the question is how much structure you get at each step, and which compromise is easiest to live with.

products.name: Amazon Basics Low-Back Armless Office Desk Chair with Back Support
products.verdict: Pneumatic height, a 360-degree swivel and sturdy construction without extras.
products.description:
This is a straightforward task chair: pneumatic seat-height adjustment, a 360-degree swivel, a back-support design and construction the listing calls sturdy. It drops the armrests so it can slide under desks that would block a standard chair.

It ranks first because it is the most conventional design in the group, and conventional is what most people need from a spare or secondary chair. The Serta below swaps in mesh for ventilation, but this one gives the clearest description of what the adjustments do and costs $50 to $100.

A shared desk or a craft table is where it earns its keep. The caveat is that a low back supports the lumbar area only, so it is not a chair for a nine-hour shift.
products.idealFor: Shared desks and secondary workspaces that need a basic, reliable seat.
products.skipIf: You sit at a desk for a full workday.

products.name: Serta Armless Small Home Desk Chair with Wheels
products.verdict: Breathable mesh and a small footprint with wheels for tight home desks.
products.description:
Serta's armless chair uses mesh material for air circulation, has an armless design, and is sold as a small home desk chair on wheels. Mesh lets heat escape from your back, which a padded fabric surface traps.

It lands second because it solves the warmth problem the Amazon Basics fabric chair does not address, but its listing gives less description of the height and swivel adjustments. It is also the clearest fit for a small home office where the chair parks under the desk.

It suits warm rooms and people who run hot. The caveat is that mesh gives less cushioning than a thick pad, so long sessions will feel firmer.
products.idealFor: People in warm rooms who want a small chair that tucks away.
products.skipIf: You want thick padding for long sits.

products.name: Orange Factory Criss Cross Chair
products.verdict: A spacious seat that lets you sit cross-legged at an armless desk.
products.description:
The Criss Cross is built around a spacious seat that lets you sit cross-legged, with an armless, space-saving design and height adjustment. An armless frame matters here because arm supports would block a crossed-leg posture.

It ranks third because it serves a narrower audience than the Amazon Basics or Serta: people who sit with their legs pulled up. For them it beats both, since a normal seat pan would force them to perch.

Choose it if you are a yoga-style sitter or work in a flexible posture. The caveat is that cross-legged sitting is hard on hips and knees for some people, so alternate your position through the day.
cons: Hard on hips if never changed
products.idealFor: Anyone who prefers to sit cross-legged while working.
products.skipIf: You sit with both feet on the floor.

products.name: OLIXIS Armless Home Office Chair
products.verdict: A Y-shaped mesh back and easy-clean seat in the $25 to $50 bucket.
products.description:
OLIXIS gives you an ergonomic Y-shaped mesh backrest, a seat described as comfortable and easy to clean, and smooth pneumatic height adjustment. The Y-shape follows the spine more closely than a flat panel.

It ranks fourth, below the Serta, because the Serta lists more clearly the small-space fit, while OLIXIS gives you a more shaped backrest for less money. It is a fair step up from the DUMOS below because the back design is specific.

Best for a budget home setup that gets daily use. The caveat is that a chair in the $25 to $50 bucket will have thinner padding and lighter components, so heavy users should look higher.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want a shaped mesh back without arms.
products.skipIf: You need a published weight capacity.

products.name: DUMOS Home Office Chair
products.verdict: A space-saving chair without armrests for the smallest desk spaces.
products.description:
DUMOS markets a space-saving design and a small office chair without armrest, with enhanced ergonomics claimed in the listing. Its small footprint is the main point: it tucks fully under a compact desk.

It ranks last because the listing gives few concrete features beyond size and the missing arms. Against OLIXIS, which names its mesh back and pneumatic lift, the DUMOS is vaguer.

Buy it for a tight dorm or a nook. The caveat is that ergonomic claims are broad, so check the product page for seat height range and weight rating before assuming it fits you.
pros: No armrests to block the desk
products.idealFor: Dorms, nooks and desks where space is the biggest constraint.
products.skipIf: You want a chair with specific lumbar or tilt features.

whatMatters.detail: A gas lift raises and lowers the seat with a lever, so your feet sit flat and your arms meet the desk at the right height. It matters more on an armless chair because there is no arm rest to compensate for a seat that is too high. Look for pneumatic in the listing, as on the Amazon Basics and OLIXIS.

Low backs stop around the lumbar area and leave your shoulders unsupported, which is fine for short sessions and poor for long ones. Mid-height mesh backs follow the spine more. Check the listing for a back dimension or the words low back, as on the Amazon Basics, before you plan a workday in it.

Mesh breathes and stays cooler, while padded fabric feels softer for a long sit. Neither is better in every case. If you run hot, the Serta or OLIXIS mesh suits you; if you want cushion, look at the Amazon Basics. Check whether the listing describes the seat as thick or breathable.

A smaller base tucks under the desk and clears tight rooms, but it can feel tippy if the legs are short. Look for a base diameter and a note on wheels. Chairs like the DUMOS and Serta emphasize size, and you should still confirm the seat does not rock when you lean.

With no arms, the chair slides fully under a desk and allows cross-legged sitting. It also removes support for resting your forearms during long typing. Check the height of your desk against the seat range, since without arms your forearm level depends entirely on the lift setting and desk height.

faq.q: Are armless chairs bad for your posture?
faq.a: Not inherently, but they remove forearm support. Pair the Amazon Basics or OLIXIS with a desk at elbow height so your arms rest on the surface, and use the pneumatic lift to set the seat correctly.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Assuming low-back means supportive. The Amazon Basics low back supports the lumbar area only, so long workdays call for a taller back. Match back height to how long you sit, not to the price.

faq.q: Is the Serta worth it over the OLIXIS?
faq.a: If you want a small chair that tucks away and a mesh seat, yes. OLIXIS costs less and has a more shaped Y back, but Serta describes the compact home-desk fit more clearly.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Assemble the base and casters first, then press in the gas lift. Set the seat so your feet are flat and thighs level. The Orange Factory and Amazon Basics both list height adjustment, so use it before sitting for long.

faq.q: How do I keep a mesh chair in good condition?
faq.a: Vacuum the mesh gently and wipe with a damp cloth. Avoid dragging sharp objects across the OLIXIS or Serta back. Check wheels for hair, which makes rolling stiff on hard floors.

faq.q: Can I use an armless chair at a standing desk?
faq.a: Yes, but check the lift range. A standing desk raised to sitting height needs a chair that goes low enough. The Criss Cross and Amazon Basics list height adjustment, but confirm the minimum before relying on it.

finalTake: The Amazon Basics Low-Back Armless chair is the one to buy for most spare desks, thanks to its pneumatic lift, full swivel and plain, sturdy build. Serta is the cooler mesh alternative, and the Orange Factory suits cross-legged sitters. OLIXIS and DUMOS are the cheapest ways to get a seat under a small desk, with less detail to back them up.
